record_notes.DCP-LETT-1604: Supplied November 19, 1854, incomplete letter. Day depends on next letter saying yesterday, while year is inferred from formal style and research interests. Cannot provide a flora of a single sterile soil; Ailsa Craig counts of seventy-nine phanerogams and sixty-eight cryptogams are only nearest approximation, and Hertfordshire sections mix soil/situation. Missing Darwin enquiry cannot be rebuilt from this answer. Quoted November 1854 Darwin diversification note is separate evidence, and circa March 1855 Balfour notes are later.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1605: November 20 with supplied 1854 year. Explicitly supplements his own letter posted yesterday, 1604; both are Watson outgoing, not a Darwin reply pair. Offers Fayal/Flores flora counts after excluding probable human introductions: 129 plus 27 equals 156, and 122 plus 22 equals 144. Area below one hundred square miles is presumed, volcanic composition observationally qualified, completeness of list likely rather than certain. Preserve tabular grouping and ferns/allies notation. Undated Darwin portfolio annotation does not establish reading on November 20.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1750: Supplied August 26, 1855 based on October 2 Watson reply. Surviving source is Darwin signed draft, not proven verbatim final sent copy. Explicitly answers August 23 numerical figure, structural comparability of genera, British flora as fragment, and expected variable-character example. Reports Gray averages 6.37 versus 4.67 and source-stated excess 1.7, compared with Watson 1.68; mathematically decimal subtraction may yield 1.70, but preserve author notation. P7 explains why he concealed the objective and now regrets it. October reply proves corresponding letter of August 26 was received by Watson, without dating dispatch/receipt precisely or proving every draft word sent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1758: October 2, 1855. Explicitly replies after delay to Darwin August 26 and quotes existing fauna/flora as mere fragment, uniquely matching draft 1750. Challenges local versus global genus sizes, distinguishes breadth of extremes from density of intermediates and number of diagnostic comparisons, then critiques inconsistent species and reproductive-organ genus classification. All seventeen body blocks and textual numerical/plant comparisons read. Separate Darwin annotations and full keyed note on reproductive organs are undated; do not treat them as Watson text or known October 2. Counterexamples and personal convictions remain qualified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1764: October 11, 1855. Sends a second marked catalogue separately from covering sheet, extending debateable forms with Babington/Newman varieties and distinguishing species-like varieties from well-defined close pairs. Gives local-versus-global comparison argument, comments on an unlocated Darwin letter mentioning Forbes, and makes Watson own accusations against Forbes. Those accusations are attributed opinion, not narrator findings. Ranunculus leaf table and hypothetical Saxifraga Andrewsii case answer or seek clarification of variable-character rule; specimen not examined, inference from description/figure only. Same-author October 2 source 1758 is not an incoming Darwin prompt. Later Darwin annotations, including yes-this-is-case, have no date here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1775: November 8, 1855. Watson remains interested but considers statistics weaker indications than Darwin does, because taxonomic groups and species judgments vary. Recommends combining 69, 195 and 32 into 296 debateable forms, with plus/equal/minus denoting probable species, possible species and probable varieties. Polygonum example distinguishes catalogue omission from biological absence of variation; hypothetical imported forms are not actual introductions. Expresses his own bias toward species not immutably distinct. Responds within ongoing correspondence but no uniquely identified surviving Darwin prompt; annotations are undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1079: Reused prior primary full reading with matching pins. Watson to Hooker, dated April 12, 1847; surviving copy made by Darwin amanuensis with Darwin heading/signature/corrections, not Darwin-authored main prose. Sixteen blocks discuss graded categories, counterexamples, qualified kail reversion and uncertain Azores Myosotis parentage. Prior accepted 1082 witness establishes Darwin read and copied it by April 18. Preserve third-party status, original date, later copy process and undated later annotations; no new target or Darwin answer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1715: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and accepted note/ledger pins. Additional full reading: Watson July 11, supplied 1855, returns Darwin Azores list with distribution markings and a second list of species least likely introduced by people. Its existence and purpose are explicit, but its complete seventy-eight entries are not transcribed here; do not invent the enclosure from the letter or Darwin twenty-two selections. P2 guesses many species arrived by human agency; P3 mentions possible Madeira transit. Footnote 2 quotes Watson marking legend, a separate voice from Darwin. Darwin salting annotation is undated. Later witness 1718 explicitly dates receipt of the list to July 13 and demonstrates using its criterion.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1740: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and accepted note/ledger pins. Additional full reading: Watson August 13, 1855, asks which kind of species to mark, contrasting Hooker and Jordan taxonomic scales. Complete separately placed Categories of Species enclosure read: four classes with Prunus, cherries, plum/sloe and bramble examples, distinctions explicitly grading into one another. Later joint Darwin/Watson wording changes quoted in footnotes and Darwin annotations are not automatically initial enclosure text/date. Marked British catalogue is not yet provided by this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1743: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and accepted note/ledger pins. Additional full reading: Watson August 17, 1855 sends marked British catalogue and distinguishes selected close pairs from species/variety entries left unmarked; warns selection may not fit unknown purpose. Independently viewed stem diagram: straight left stalk and right stalk curved at base, illustrating Drosera distinction; no species labels or scale printed in image. Physical catalogue and separate pre-1847 publication list are not fully transcribed. Later October/November calculations and Natural selection counts in apparatus are not August body. Courtesy and phrenology comment remain Watson voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1747: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and accepted note/ledger pins. Additional full reading: Watson August 23, 1855 responds to unlocated disclosure of Darwin numerical objective and Fries remark. Says prior marking was illustrative rather than numerically exact; British small genera can be globally large. Two textual diagrams compare equal extreme separation with denser intermediate species versus extreme separation scaling with species count; retain rows and many/few labels, not linear prose. Argues taxonomic grouping partly human and small-flora statistics weak indications. Future Saxifraga example postponed; Darwin marginal rebuttals are undated. This criticism does not itself demonstrate Darwin read it by August 24 merely because topics recur.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Viewed preserved image: two drawn flowering stalks, the left long and straight, the right with conspicuously curved basal end. No printed labels or scale. Illustrates the straight versus curved-at-base diagnostic character discussed for Drosera; do not assign species labels solely from the unlabelled drawing.

reading_method: Six targets independently read in full, including original XML date attributes, bodies, tables, draft text, exclusions, all scholarly annotations and bibliography. Four target sources reuse explicit primary readings from batches 10/12; third-party context 1079 reuses verified 1847 primary source. The viewed 1743 figure and source pins are carried from accepted batch-10.
